subject: Communication
title: Ethnocentrism: The Default Bias
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Ethnocentrism: The Default Bias.

hook.text: Every culture thinks it's normal and others are strange. That's not an insult — it's a cognitive default called ethnocentrism.

buildup.text: Ethnocentrism means judging other cultures by the standards of your own — often unconsciously.

discovery.text: It's evolutionarily wired: in-group preference helped survival.

twist.text: The antidote isn't cultural relativism (all practices are equal). It's cultural humility: 'My way isn't the only way.'

climax.text: Moving from ethnocentrism to ethnorelativism — appreciating other cultural logics — is a process, not a switch to flip.

punchline.text: Your normal is someone else's strange. And vice versa.

quiz.question: What is ethnocentrism?
options: Judging other cultures by your own standards

details.summary: Ethnocentrism is the unconscious tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of your own, assuming your way is normal and others are deviations. It is the default human condition and the primary barrier to effective cross-cultural communication.
details.whyItMatters: Until you recognize your own ethnocentrism, every cultural difference looks like the other person doing something wrong rather than something different.
takeaways: Ethnocentrism judges other cultures by your own standards
It is an unconscious default, not a deliberate choice
Recognizing it is the first step to cross-cultural competence

faq.question: How do you recognize your own ethnocentrism?
faq.answer: Notice when you label foreign practices as 'weird,' 'wrong,' or 'inefficient.' These judgments often signal ethnocentric framing. Ask yourself whether the practice serves a function within its cultural context. Travel, reading, and diverse friendships accelerate this awareness.

faq.question: Is it possible to completely eliminate ethnocentrism?
faq.answer: Probably not entirely. Cultural programming runs deep and some in-group preference appears to be neurologically wired. The goal is not elimination but awareness and management. Recognizing ethnocentric reactions when they arise gives you the choice to override them.
